discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed in 650f46cf7. `runCloud` now reports failures through `writeErr` as well, so every `--cloud --json` failure (startup checks and dispatch) is the same `{"type":"error"}` record. The custom `cloud_error` type is gone and the README says so.

Fixed in https://github.com/cline/cline/commit/e1a1e179ecbfa2f593f7e1272aa8fa2dcc1986f6.

`run_commands`, `editor`, and `apply_patch` return `success: false` without setting `isError`, and `run_commands` returns an array of those records. `scanTurn` and `summarizeTurn` now treat that as a failure, drop the edit, and keep the error text. The check is in https://github.com/cline/cline/commit/ad07813118d7efbd12631ab36a34fa8de24a9215 on https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/15388.

*medium*

`.then(attach, onError)` catches a rejected spawn but not an exception thrown inside `attach` itself (stream setup, the Bun socket check). That becomes an unhandled rejection and the synthetic child never fails or closes, so the command can sit until the outer timeout. `.then(attach).catch(fail)` covers both.

*medium*

`MxcProcess.kill()` calls `throwIfFailed(this.native.kill(...))`, so it throws on a non-zero status. `SandboxedProcess.kill` doesn't catch, and the caller in `bash.ts` ignores the promise from `killProcessTree().finally(...)`, so a failed kill becomes an unhandled rejection in the CLI or extension host and can terminate it depending on the runtime's unhandled-rejection setting. Wrap it and route the error through `fail`.

Valid, and fixed in b6807e2ab. When `createCheckpoint` throws, the hook records a failure for that run, then rethrows, so the existing error behavior is unchanged. Recording is best effort, so a failed metadata write can't replace the original error. Covered by `records a failure, then rethrows, when a custom checkpoint throws` in `checkpoint-hooks.test.ts`.

Valid, and fixed in 1690c40bf. `SessionVersioningService` now passes `restoreWorkspace` to `createCheckpointRestorePlan`. A recorded failure blocks only a file restore; a chat-only restore anchors to the nearest earlier checkpoint, as it did before this PR. Covered by `refuses to restore files for a run whose checkpoint failed, but rewinds chat` in `checkpoint-restore.test.ts`.

While checking this, I found the same problem in the desktop app's edit-message fork, which still used `findCheckpointForRun` and would have restored the previous run's snapshot. It now uses `resolveRunCheckpoint` and keeps the current files for a failed run, covered by a new test in `chat-session.test.ts`.

discussion_comments.comment_body:
Blocker: this drops provider details for unrecoverable context-overflow failures.

`ContextWindowOverflowError` wraps the provider message (`"... (provider reported: prompt is too long)"`), so it never equals `lastError` and `lastModelFailure` is cleared. Verified on `ecb3332a` with a gateway model returning a 400 overflow failure: the terminal `sdk.error` only has `error_type: ContextWindowOverflowError` (no `error_status`, `error_code`, `errorPhase`, `aiSdkCallId`, `requestId`), and `result.error.cause` is `undefined`. Before this PR the provider layer reported those fields, so this is a telemetry regression on a high-volume failure class.

Suggested fix:

```ts
if (
	!(normalized instanceof ContextWindowOverflowError) &&
	normalized.message !== this.state.lastError
)
	this.state.lastModelFailure = undefined;
```

A test asserting `error_status` / `errorPhase` on the overflow `sdk.error` would lock it in. 🔍

Valid finding. I confirmed that `routeToTeammate()` can resolve with `finishReason: "error"`, and the async execution path explicitly checks for this case in `multi-agent.ts`.

The sync path currently drops `finishReason` and would report `status: "completed"` even for a failed model stream. The underlying error handling was already missing, but the new status makes that failure appear successful.

Let's add the same `finishReason === "error"` guard to the sync path and a regression test before merging.

🟢 **bug** (low)

`CheckpointTracker.commit()` rejects on failure (`throw new Error(`Failed to create checkpoint: ...`)`), and previously that rejection was awaited inside the block that appears to be swallowed by the enclosing `// silently fails for now` handler. The detached promise now has no `.catch()`, so any commit failure becomes an unhandled promise rejection, and overlapping commits make failures (e.g. git index lock contention) more likely. In addition, `checkpoint_created` is now always said, so a failed commit leaves the chat showing a checkpoint message with no hash and no hint that anything went wrong.

**建议**: Attach an error handler that logs (same intent as the previous silent failure), e.g. `.catch((error) => console.error("Failed to save checkpoint:", error))`, or store the promise and await it inside the existing try/catch so errors keep the old behaviour.

Valid, and introduced by the previous revision. Fixed by killing the child when its stdin write fails: the connection is dead at that point regardless, and the exit handler then fails the pending requests at once. A server that already exited keeps its real exit status, so the exit-code report Dom asked for is unchanged. Added a test with a server that closes stdin but stays alive; it rejects within milliseconds rather than at the request timeout.

Valid, but not introduced here: the manager never re-checks a client after `connect()`, so any stdio server whose process dies leaves it cached as connected. A server that simply crashes on a tool call reproduces it on main: the first call reports the exit, every later call fails with "not connected". On main the stdin-closed case ends there too, since the broken stdin makes every request fail as not connected. Making the manager respawn a client that lost its process is a separate change, tracked as a follow-up.

Fixed in b7fd827e5b. Command timeouts now use a coalesced, bounded client.list health probe. A successful probe or any other command reply arriving during it keeps the socket and SSH forward alive; only a failed probe with no intervening replies retires the transport. Regression tests cover a slow read with an unrelated pending write, a slow heartbeat while writes receive replies, concurrent timeout probe coalescing, and the real one-way forwarding stall. Writes and prompts are never replayed.
Agreed, fixed. The probe handler now stores the parse failure and rejects pending sends with it on close, so a caller sees the same cause NodeHubClient reports instead of the generic close message.
Fixed, now Buffer.byteLength(text). Cheap and the byte count is the number we want if this turns out to be a size threshold.

Fixed — a recovered turn now also requires non-empty content: a `stop`/`tool-calls` finish with an empty message records `phase: failed` with `eventType: empty_response` (and the failure notice says so), matching the loop's emptiness rejection. Covered by a new test. Branch is also rebased onto latest main.

Fixed — the loop's acceptance rule (non-empty content, or provider-executed model-tool activity in metadata) is now extracted into a single `hasRenderableTurnOutput` helper used by both the loop's emptiness check and the recovery outcome classification, so the two can no longer drift. A retry whose only output is model-tool activity records `succeeded`. Covered by a new test.

Valid — fixed, test-first: both `stop` and `max-tokens` empty retries reproduced exactly this (`Model returned empty response`, truncated turn gone). An empty retry is no more a replacement than an aborted or errored one, so it now keeps the truncated turn and lets the loop surface the max-tokens error, matching the nothing-to-compact path. Also added a table-driven test over the full retry-outcome matrix (every finish reason × text / tool call / empty / provider-executed activity) asserting the partial answer is never silently dropped and the loop is never handed an empty turn — all 20 cells pass.

**[P2] Preserve transient provider retries.** If the compacted request returns an empty error with `errorRetryable: true`, this throw bypasses `generateAssistantMessageWithProviderRetry` and fails the run immediately. Please let the compacted request use the existing bounded provider retry policy.

Fixed — an errored retry that ran a provider tool or emitted text is now recorded alongside the truncated turn before the failure surfaces (matching how the loop records such a turn before failing); only a retry that produced nothing is dropped. Test asserts the retry message specifically survives with its activity.
